title: Tibetan Yoga and Secret Doctrines, or Seven Books of Wisdom of the Great Path
author: ed. W. Y. Evans-Wentz (Six Yogas of Naropa material and other texts)
edition_cited: First edition, London: Oxford University Press (Humphrey Milford), 1935; DLI scan in.ernet.dli.2015.24914
tradition: Kagyu (Six Yogas of Naropa: psychic heat, illusory body); Mahamudra
locator_hints: Book III ch. I, Psychic Heat, Preliminary Exercise 1 (paras 13-16, pp. 173-175): Vajra-Yogini visualization, size expansion and reduction

Book III ch. II, Illusory Body, 'The Maya of the Visualizing State' (paras 7-13, pp. 210-212): painted Vajrasattva in a mirror, figure appears animated; footnote on the 'standard test' that the visualization becomes life-like/substantial
Same chapter paras 14-19: sky gazing, Five Signs, vision of Buddha form against cloudless sky
General Introduction X, 'Psychology of the Yogic Visualizations' (pp. 44-45)
Book II Yoga of One-Pointedness paras 32-34 (p. 124-125): image/picture or visualization of Buddha in front
summary: Kazi Dawa-Samdup's translations of Six Yogas manuals with Evans-Wentz's notes. In the Illusory Body yoga the practitioner places a painted image of Vajrasattva so it is reflected in a mirror, gazes at the reflection with fixity of gaze and mind until the figure appears animated, then visualizes it as standing between mirror and self; if this visualization becomes substantial enough to touch, he extends it to other bodies and to all visible forms. The editor's footnote calls life-likeness 'the standard test applied to yogic visualizations'. The Psychic-Heat preliminaries visualize oneself as Vajra-Yogini, transparent and radiant, expanded to the size of the universe and reduced to a sesame seed with all parts sharply defined. Book II offers an image, a picture, or a visualized Buddha placed in front of one as concentration supports. Elsewhere the deity is declared purely mind-produced.
why_relevant: Explicit open-eye bridge from a gazed painted image to a visualized form located in the space in front of the practitioner, with a stated criterion of success (animated, life-like, touchable).

date_evidence.basis: archive.org metadata for in.ernet.dli.2015.24914 gives 1935; scan is the OUP first edition

notes: Published 1935, so treated as in copyright under the run rule; only excerpts (with original OCR line numbers) are saved, no verbatim quotes recorded. Notes by Evans-Wentz mix in Theosophical and parapsychological glosses (e.g. 'materializations').
